mathematical_delta.actual_objects: C is the exact dyadic interpretation of the caller's original finite float64 raw cores. D is the exact dyadic interpretation of the SAME returned cores, and s is Fraction.from_float(actual mantissa)*2^actual exponent from the SAME ScaledNorm return. It is not an ideal scale product, float-expanded normalizer or alternative exact canonicalizer.
mathematical_delta.local_recursion: crossGram(nil,nil)=1; crossGram(cons A C,cons B D)=sum bit, A_bit*crossGram(C,D)*B_bit^T. Each update uses two matrix products, not a naive four-index contraction. Different dependent left/right bond dimensions are supported.
mathematical_delta.full_semantics: crossGram_eq_sum proves equality with sum over every physical word of contract(C,word)*contract(D,word)^T. For scalar boundaries its00 entry is the complete inner product. Exponential word enumeration appears only in this specification, never the checker.
mathematical_delta.computed_residual: q=G_D-2*cross(C,D)/s+G_C/s^2 equals ||vector(D)-vector(C)/s||^2 exactly. This end-to-end residual includes initial rescaling, QR, residual rescaling, absorption, head division, underflow and rounded ScaleProduct drift; no blanket NumPy theorem is assumed.
mathematical_delta.computed_normalizer: a2=G_C/s^2. Since a=sqrt(G_C)/s>=0, |a-1|<=|a^2-1|. Set tau=abs(a2-1) exactly and obtain the actual inverse-normalizer error without pretending s is the source norm.
mathematical_delta.directed_root: For q>=0, ceil(q*2^(2b)) is integer-square-rooted upward, producing r=m/2^b with a final exact check r^2>=q. Zero and exact-grid ties are covered; no float residual is used as an upper bound.
mathematical_delta.output_bound: certificate_to_normalized proves ||vector(D)-normalize(vector(C))||<=r+tau, requiring only internally supplied s>0,r>=0,G_C>0 and the two exact computed inequalities. No normalized-output, orthogonality or rank premise is hidden.
mathematical_delta.signed_scope: Literal vector subtraction on the full physical Word n carrier; no phase alignment or absolute-amplitude comparison. This TT theorem does not introduce ancillas. A circuit consumer must still bound its whole signed state, including every garbage sector, relative to this actual returned TT.
